title: Prompts: Templates That Package Expertise
objective: After this lesson you will be able to author MCP prompts (reusable interaction templates with arguments), decide prompt-vs-tool-vs-resource per need, and version templates alongside the servers they steer.
why: Every team re-derives the same triage instructions, classification rubrics, and review checklists per conversation. MCP prompts package them server-side: user-driven templates (slash-command style) with typed arguments, discoverable via prompts/list, rendered via prompts/get. Expertise ships once, used everywhere — the few-shot packs from Prompt 101, distributed.

blocks.text: MCP **prompts** are reusable message templates with **arguments** (e.g. `triage-ticket` taking `ticket`): clients list them, users pick (often as slash commands), servers render filled messages. Unlike tools (model-invoked actions) or resources (data), prompts are *human-initiated interaction patterns* — the team's best triage rubric, review checklist, or classification few-shots, maintained in one place.

blocks.caption: Arguments in, rendered messages out — expertise on tap

blocks.text: Prompt vs tool vs resource (final routing)

Three-way routing completes the primitive map: **human initiates a pattern** → prompt (slash commands, rubrics, checklists). **Model needs data** → resource (policy text, catalog rows). **Model must act/compute** → tool (lookups, refunds). Misplacements cost: prompts doing live lookups (stale by render time), tools serving static text (latency + reasoning waste), resources holding actions (unexecutable context).

blocks.title: Prompts are team assets
blocks.text: A prompt pack (system + few-shots + contracts from Prompt 101) ports directly into MCP prompts: same content, distributed delivery. Maintain packs in version control, render through prompts/get, and test with the gold sets that already exist — no duplication between 'prompt engineering' and 'MCP prompts'.

blocks.title: Route the primitive
blocks.note: Run it: expect 5/5. Three-way routing (pattern/data/action) completes the primitive map from Ch.4 — every MCP addition starts with this question.

items: Prompts package team expertise as user-driven templates with typed arguments
Three-way routing: human-pattern → prompt; stable-data → resource; compute/live/act → tool
Version templates with their servers; unchanged prompts across server versions lie about capabilities

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice router and confirm 5/5. (b) Author a review-checklist prompt (arguments: draft text; renders length/tone/offer checks) in the v2 shape with one-line rationale per check. (c) State what breaks when the prompt stays v1 while its server ships v2 tools.
hints: Baseline 5/5; each case exercises one routing rule including the clarify fallback.
Checklist prompt: argsSchema {draft}, messages encoding the three checks — mirrors the Prompt 101 verifier as a distributed template.
Stale prompts reference renamed tools/dead fields: template-server version skew produces confident misdirection — version together.
exercise.why: Template authoring (expertise packaged) plus primitive routing (pattern/data/action) plus co-versioning (templates track servers) are the three prompt judgments.
exercise.code: // Prompt template: args in, rendered checklists out, versioned with server.

quiz.q: Triage rubric used by five teammates, copy-pasted per chat. MCP shape?
options: Prompt: user-driven reusable template with ticket argument — maintained once, discovered via list
quiz.explain: Human-initiated patterns belong in prompts: discoverable, versioned, consistent across the team. Copy-paste is the pre-protocol symptom.

quiz.q: Live inventory count as a prompt. Verdict?
options: Misuse: live data needs tool calls (fresh per invocation); prompts render static patterns, not live reads
quiz.explain: Prompts template interactions; they don't fetch. Live needs belong to tools with fresh execution per call.

quiz.q: Prompt v1 references tool names renamed in server v2. Fix?
options: Co-version templates with servers: stale prompts misdirect confidently; version together, test together
quiz.explain: Template-server skew produces confident misdirection (right pattern, dead names). Versioning binds them; tests prove the binding.

summary: Prompts distribute team expertise as versioned, user-driven templates. Route pattern/data/action correctly; co-version templates with servers.
